item.title: Amazon Bedrock Adds Agentic Retrieval to Managed Knowledge Base
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Adds Agentic Retrieval to Managed Knowledge Base

Amazon Bedrock’s Managed Knowledge Base now supports agentic retrieval, an advanced RAG capability that plans and iterates over search steps automatically.

🔍 Overview

  • Agentic retrieval is available on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.
  • Instead of one search, Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base plans the retrieval.
  • It breaks the question into sub‑queries, runs them, judges whether it has enough evidence, and searches again if it doesn’t.
  • Two APIs are provided:
    • Retrieve – runs one hybrid search and returns scored chunks.
    • AgenticRetrieveStream – runs a planning loop and streams the steps back to you as trace events.

🧩 How it works

  • The planner splits the user query into sub‑queries.
  • Each sub‑query is executed against the knowledge base.
  • After each step the system checks whether the accumulated evidence is sufficient.
  • If not, additional sub‑queries are generated and the process repeats.
  • When a passage lacks enough context, a FullDocumentExpansion step calls bedrock:GetDocumentContent to fetch the whole document.

⚙️ Integration with LangChain

  • The langchain-aws package exposes both retrieval modes.
    • The standard Retrieve API appears as a normal LangChain retriever that can be dropped into a chain.
    • The AgenticRetrieveStream API is exposed as a function retrieval directly from a knowledge base.
  • Both paths return document chunks from the knowledge base, which the application then uses to generate a grounded response.

📦 Key Details

  • Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base removes the self‑managed vector store, embeddings, and re‑ranking models from the RAG architecture.
  • You configure a data source (e.g., an Amazon S3 bucket); the service handles chunking, embedding, storage, and retrieval.
  • Boto3 version 1.43.32 or later is required; agentic_retrieve_stream did not exist before that version.
  • The knowledge base assumes a service role with the following permissions:
    • bedrock:GetDocumentContent (often overlooked)
    • s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:GetObject on its contents, both conditioned on aws:ResourceAccount
    • If guardrails are used, also bedrock:GetGuardrail and bedrock:ApplyGuardrail
  • A policy with only bedrock:Retrieve works until the planner reaches a whole‑document fetch, then fails.

🚀 Availability & Costs

  • The walkthrough uses the US East (N. Virginia) Region (us-east-1).
  • Running the walkthrough may incur costs for document storage, ingestion, retrieval calls, and foundation model inference.
  • Delete the resources when you complete the experiment to avoid ongoing charges.

📊 API Comparison

API Behavior
Retrieve Runs one hybrid search and returns scored chunks.
AgenticRetrieveStream Executes a planning loop, streams each step as trace events, and returns document chunks after iterative retrieval.

#AmazonBedrock #AgenticRetrieval #RAG #LangChain #AWS

Source: Agentic retrieval with LangChain and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Evolution of AI Agent Frameworks and Specialized Coding Tools for 2026
item.description:
Evolution of AI Agent Frameworks and Specialized Coding Tools for 2026

The landscape of AI development has expanded into specialized orchestration frameworks and diverse coding tools. Developers now choose between low-level graph-based execution, role-based multi-agent crews, and specialized IDE-integrated agents, often supported by routers to manage model lock-in and costs.

🔍 Framework Overview

Modern frameworks provide different levels of abstraction for building stateful agents and multi-agent workflows. These tools range from code-first toolkits to low-level orchestration frameworks that ensure durable execution.

Tool Primary Focus Language Support
LangChain Stateful agents as graphs with durable execution Python, JavaScript/TypeScript
CrewAI Multi-agent teams with role-based agents and Flows Python (3.10 to 3.13)
OpenAI Multi-agent workflows with handoffs and tracing OpenAI models
Anthropic SDK Claude Code tools, agent loop, and context management Python, TypeScript
Microsoft Successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel C#, Python, Go (preview)
Google Code-first toolkit for building and deploying agents Python, TS, Go, Java, Kotlin
LlamaIndex Document ingestion, retrieval, and RAG Python
Posh Native TypeScript framework with web integrations TypeScript

⚙️ Key Details

Selection depends on the specific technical requirements of the agent or workflow:

  • LangChain: A low-level framework focusing on durable execution that recovers from failures. It requires more time to learn due to its low-level API.
  • CrewAI: Features a simple role and task model for multi-agent teams using event-driven Flows for workflow control.
  • OpenAI: Offers a lightweight, open-source framework with a small set of building blocks that are easy to learn, prioritizing OpenAI models.
  • LlamaIndex: Provides deep tooling for document ingestion and retrieval; however, its TypeScript version was deprecated in April 2026.
  • Posh: Integrates natively with Next.js, React, Express, and Hono, requiring Node.js 22.18 or later.
  • Anthropic SDK: Packages tools for files, shell, and web search, specifically for use with Claude models.

🚀 Coding Tool Selection

Choosing the right AI coding tool depends on where the developer wants the AI to live—whether in the terminal, woven into the editor, or as a standalone IDE.

Tool Category Best Use Case
Claude Code Terminal agent Agentic, multi-file CLI work
Codex Terminal agent OpenAI-centric agentic coding
Cursor AI-native IDE In-editor edits and inline chat
Windsurf AI-native IDE Editor workflows and agentic flows
Cline In-editor agent VS Code agent with model choice
Wuwei Router Accessing multiple models via one entry

💡 Model Flexibility and Cost

While many tools lock developers to one provider’s models and billing, routers like Wuwei remove these constraints. A router allows terminal agents like Claude Code or Codex to reach Claude, GPT, Grok, Gemini, Kimi, and DeepSeek from a single endpoint. This approach enables routing routine work to cheaper models while reserving premium models for difficult problems. For low cost across models, pay-as-you-go routers allow the use of cheap models only when necessary without per-provider subscriptions.

#AIagents #LangChain #ClaudeCode #SoftwareDevelopment #OpenSource

Source: Best AI Agent Frameworks (2026): LangGraph, CrewAI and More Source: Best AI Coding Tools in 2026 (Tested & Compared)

item.title: AI Engineer Role Focused on LangChain, RAG, and Model Context Protocols
item.description:
AI Engineer Role Focused on LangChain, RAG, and Model Context Protocols

A pioneer in smart connected technology, precision agriculture, and autonomous machinery is opening a 12‑month contract for an AI Engineer to join its Enterprise Data Science & AI Enablement team.

🔍 Overview

  • The position is centered on translating departmental AI use cases into scalable, reusable AI agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) connections, Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, and modular starter kits.

⚙️ Role & Responsibilities

  • Architect, build, and maintain a central repository of reusable AI skills, agentic workflows, prompt templates, and developer starter kits.
  • Build and deploy functional AI agents, tool‑calling chains, and conversational copilots using Python and frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or AutoGen.
  • Implement and standardize Model Context Protocols (MCPs) and custom tool harnesses to connect large language models (LLMs) securely with internal databases, APIs, and document stores.
  • Design and optimize RAG pipelines, embedding strategies, semantic search indices, and vector‑database storage for contextual reasoning.
  • Partner with embedded AI coaches across departments to package one‑off solutions into reusable, well‑documented enterprise knowledge assets.
  • Establish automated testing harnesses, evaluate agent performance and output quality, track adoption metrics, and manage version‑controlled releases via GitHub.

📍 Location & Work Structure

  • Locations: Austin, TX 78704; Chicago, IL; Urbandale, IA – open to 100 % fully remote work.
  • Shift: First Shift, standard daytime business hours (≈ 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM), Monday through Friday.

💰 Compensation & Contract

  • Pay Rate: $56.00 – $60.00 per hour on a W‑2 basis.
  • Contract Duration: 12 months with the possibility of extension.
  • Seniority Level: Mid‑Senior.
  • Employment Type: Full‑time.
  • Industries: Motor Vehicle Manufacturing, Industrial Machinery Manufacturing, and Manufacturing.

🛠️ Required Skills & Technologies

  • 4 + years of software/data engineering experience with generative AI systems, conversational agents, or LLM‑powered applications.
  • Expert‑level Python development and familiarity with standard data/AI libraries.
  • Hands‑on experience orchestrating LLMs using LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, AutoGen, or comparable agent frameworks.\n- Practical understanding of Model Context Protocols (MCPs), API tool calling, and dynamic context injection.
  • Experience building end‑to‑end RAG pipelines and working with vector databases such as Pinecone, Milvus, Chroma, Weaviate, Qdrant, or pgvector.
  • Advanced GitHub workflow, CI/CD automation, and test‑harness engineering.
  • Cloud engineering experience on AWS (Bedrock, SageMaker, Lambda, S3).
  • Experience with complex multi‑agent systems, big‑data platforms (Databricks, Spark, Delta Lake), and developer documentation.

📅 Application Process

  • A mandatory Glider AI/Coding assessment must be completed before client submission.
  • Interested candidates should contact the recruiter at jevin@cube-hub.com.

#AIEngineering #LangChain #RAG #EnterpriseAI

item.title: Development of a RAG-enabled Chatbot using LangChain and LLaMA
item.description:
Development of a RAG-enabled Chatbot using LangChain and LLaMA

A new RAG-powered chatbot implementation has been developed using LangChain to orchestrate an LLaMA model and NVIDIA embeddings. The system is designed to provide context-aware responses by retrieving relevant documentation from a FAISS-backed vector store.

🧩 How it works

The system processes information by generating embeddings for documents, storing them in a FAISS index, and retrieving context for the LLaMA model during query generation. The pipeline supports both basic and RAG-enabled reasoning, with performance verified through LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation techniques.

⚙️ Key details

Component Function
LangChain Orchestrates LLM components and pipeline chaining
LLaMa Handles text generation based on retrieved context
FAISS Enables efficient similarity search and document retrieval
NVIDIA Embeddings Generates vector representations of documents
FastAPI Exposes the pipeline via RESTful APIs
Gradio Provides an interactive frontend for user testing

📂 Project Structure

  • server_app.py: FastAPI server implementation
  • 08_evaluation.ipynb: RAG pipeline implementation
  • docstore_index/: FAISS document store directory
  • frontend/: Gradio interface code
  • requirements.txt: Project dependencies

#RAG #LangChain #LLaMA #FastAPI #FAISS

Source: misterseyiayeni/retrieval-augmented-generation
